To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a low dose of the NMDA channel blocker, MK-801, impairs primed burst potentization in the dentate of freely moving rats, and that this dose also impairs spatial learning but not performance in the radial eight-arm maze.

the low doses of MK-801 (0.125-0.5 mg/kg ip) that impair spatial learning in rats also reduce the frequency and amplitude of hippocampally generated RSA and reduce normal synaptic transmission from entorhinal cortical to dentate gyrus synapses, and that the same doses of MK- 801 attenuate primed burst potentiaiton in the dentate granule cells.
a dose of MK801 (1 mg/kg) previously shown to impair radial maze learning also reduces primed burst potentiated synaptic transmission in the dentate of freely moving rats.

the neurobiological basis of spatial cognition.
the effects of MK801 on spatial learning in rats.
the effects of NMDA receptor antagonists on hippocampal function and spatial behavior.

MK801, in a dose previously shown to impair learning in the radial arm maze, attenuates primed-burst potentiation in the freely moving rat.

the low dose of MK-801 used in the current study did impair spatial learning and reduced synaptic plasticity in behaving rats.

the low dose of MK-801 disrupts spatial learning by impairing synaptic plasticity in a manner that is not dependent on a reduction in the frequency of hippocampal RSA.
the low doses of MK-801 impair learning by reducing synaptic plasticity.

low doses of MK 801, which impair spatial learning, also reduce the likelihood of synaptic potentiation in the same pathway.
the hippocampus is a critical site for the action of MK-801, and that the effect of MK-801 in the hippocampus is to reduce synaptic plasticity.
